1_Learning_Objective.Title: 🎯 The "Why Are We Learning This?" (Learning Objective)
1_Learning_Objective.Content: The goal is to teach your child the concept of singular (one) and plural (more than one or 'many'). They will learn the basic grammar rule of adding the magic letter 's' to the end of words to show there are many!

2_The_Hook.Title: 🪝 The Hook (How to start the conversation)
2_The_Hook.Content: Hold up a single crayon and say: **'I have one crayon.'** Then grab a whole handful of crayons and say: **'Now I have a lot of crayon... wait, that sounds funny! We don't say five crayon. What do we say?'** (Let them answer 'crayons!'). **'Exactly! We have to add a snake sound at the end to show there are many!'**

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'When we only have one of something, the word stays the same. One cat. But when we have two, three, or a hundred, we use magic! We add the letter S to the end. Two cats!'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Have them hold one pencil. Say 'One pencil.' Hand them three more. Say 'Now add the magic S! Four pencils!'

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Let's use our listening ears. When you hear the snake sound (ssss) at the end of a word, you know it means there are many.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Call out words like 'Apples', 'Dog', 'Cars', 'Book'. Have them jump if they hear it's 'many' (has an S) or stand still if it's 'one'.

Mini_Lessons.Topic: Lesson 3: One vs. Many in Sentences
Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'We match our words. We say "I see one bird." We say "I see many birds."'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Look out the window or at a picture book. Say, 'Look, there is one tree, but over there are many trees.'

4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Title: 🚧 Common Stumbling Blocks (What to watch out for)
4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Content:
Irregular plurals (like child/children, mouse/mice, tooth/teeth). Children will naturally try to say 'childs' or 'tooths' because they learned the 's' rule.
*   **How to clarify:** Smile and say, 'You used the magic S rule beautifully! But a few words like to be silly and break the rules. The many word for tooth is teeth!' Don't stress too much on irregulars right now; just gently correct as they come up.

Questions.Question: If I have one book, and you give me two more, do I have three book or three books?
What is the 'many' word for Star?
If I say 'The boys are playing', is there just one boy, or many boys?

Activities.Name: 1. The Magic Wand
Activities.Description: Give them a pencil to use as a 'magic wand'. Lay out single items (one block, one shoe, one spoon). Have them wave the wand, add more items to the pile, and shout the new 'many' word (Blocks! Shoes! Spoons!).

Activities.Name: 2. One and Many Baskets
Activities.Description: Get two bowls. Label one 'One' and the other 'Many'. Give them a mix of small items (1 coin, 3 buttons, 1 lego, 5 beads) and have them sort them into the correct bowls while saying the words out loud.

Activities.Name: 3. Silly Drawings
Activities.Description: Fold a paper in half. On one side, write 'One Monster' and draw one monster. On the other side, write 'Many Monsters' and have your child draw 5 silly monsters.
